newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares finish higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares finish higher in thin trade.

text.p: * Volume of shares traded 3.2 bln valued at 1.7 bln pesos
Manila shares ended higher after a lacklustre session for the second straight day on Wednesday as traders said the market remained cautious despite the Dow's gains.
"The inability of the market to catch up with the recovery of the Dow indicates an underlying weakness," said Joey Salceda, director at SBC Warburg.
The main index finished 11.51 points up at 2,960.97.
The volume of trade was still way below the 2.9 billion peso daily average, traders said.
Diversified Securities Inc executive vice-president Jose Ricardo Garcia said the market would remain shaky until the 3,000 resistance level was pierced.
Traders said reaction to Ayala Land's first quarter 15 percent rise in profits to 1.42 billion pesos was muted with the stock gaining only 50 centavos to 26 pesos.
In the broader market, losers outnumbered gainers 57 to 43 with 96 unchanged issues.
"We will likely see more of the same market as underweighting of banks and the property sector remains the central theme to foreign investors," said SBC's Salceda.
Diversified's Garcia said the market would likely tread in a narrow band for the rest of the week taking cue from the Dow.
